newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Parmalat to invest $17 mln in Venezuelan milk.
newsitem.headline: Parmalat to invest $17 mln in Venezuelan milk.

text.p: Italy's Parmalat Finanziara SpA said Tuesday it would invest $17 million to upgrade its Venezuelan milk processing plants in a boost to improve margins after milk consumption fell 30 percent last year.
"We are in the midst of a restructuring process," Venezuelan company president Adrianus Boer told Congress.

Boer was summoned to Congress to explain reports published last week that the company was closing milk plants throughout the country, fanning discontent in an already hard pressed, but politically well-connected, dairy sector.

"With this new investment, Parmalat is increasing its stake in Venezuela," countered Boer, who said that only one of its seven plants would be closed, and then only temporarily while demand remained slack.

Boer said the company planned to increase milk purchases to 1.2 million liters a day, from current levels of 900,000 liters. He added, however, that the Venezuelan farmers had to improve efficiency if they wanted to avoid higher import penetration.

Venezuela traditionally imports some 40 percent of its annual milk needs, industry figures show, but cheap imports ratcheted- up nationalist rhetoric last year bringing a two month import ban to Zulia state that produces the bulk of the nation's milk.
Parmlat controls 60 percent of the Venezuelan milk market after it bought a controlling stake in state-owned milk company Indulac in 1995 for $14.7 million in 1995.
